Koba the Dread: Laughter and the Twenty Million is a 2002 non-fiction book by British writer Martin Amis .

Summary

[ edit ]
The book is a study of the depredations of the regime of Joseph Stalin in the Soviet Union from the 1920s to the 1950s. The title alludes to Stalin's nickname "Koba", and the estimated 20 million deaths in the Soviet Union during Stalin's rule owing to starvation, torture, gulags , and the purges and confessions of

...

The Leningrad-born American writer Gary Shteyngart called Koba "harrowing and strangely funny" in The Washington Post , explaining: "'Koba the Dread' is not easy to forget.

...

The book occasioned a public schism between Amis and fellow writer and close friend Christopher Hitchens , [ 9 ] [ 10 ] especially in the pages of The Atlantic , where Hitchens described Koba the Dread as "Stalinism without irony". [ 11 ] The break was later mended. [ 12 ]
